commits.messageBody:
The shared session store rewrites the whole of sessions.json (12 MB on
a long-lived install) on every mapping change. It did so with
writeFileSync, fsyncSync, renameSync and a synchronous directory fsync
on the event loop, and lock retries slept in Atomics.wait. One fsync
waits for the filesystem's journal commit: about 20 ms on an idle disk,
0.2-0.6 s under ordinary load, and on a busy disk long enough that the
proxy answered nothing for up to 106 s - no /health, no reads from open
streams - and the turns streaming at the time failed as "Upstream
stalled".

The store now takes the same steps through fs/promises, in the same
order, while holding the lock: write the temporary file, sync it,
rename it over the store, sync the directory. The lock file is written
and synced once per acquisition and re-linked on each attempt, as the
session-GC sidecar lock already does, and a retry waits on a timer.
Nothing is renamed before its contents are durable, so crash safety is
unchanged.

Within one process, mutations of a store run one at a time in call
order, so an overlapping later write cannot land before an earlier
one; the lock file still arbitrates between processes. The request
handler runs its own store transactions in order as well, including
the eviction a client disconnect triggers, so a cancel acts on the
state an in-flight publication leaves behind, and a streamed turn ends,
releasing its session, only after that eviction has landed - as when
the eviction ran inside cancel() itself. A request waits for the store
writes this process has already started before it takes its arrival
snapshot, so an eviction a cancelled stream left behind is visible to
the session's next request, as it was when every write finished before
anything else could run.

The store mutators, pruneSupersededProfileCopies() among them, and
clearSessionCache() exported from the package, now return promises;
releaseSupersededProfileCopies() awaits the prune while it still holds
the lifecycle lock and the turn leases.

commits.messageBody:
Resolves the conflicts with #1480 and #1476:

- session/cache.ts: the interrupted-turn record is cleared and set in
  the store-mutation continuations, under the commit epoch, like the
  rest of the cache effects. markSessionInterrupted goes through
  mapStoreMutation, since the JSON store's writes may now be
  asynchronous; interrupted-turn-cache.test.ts awaits it.
- server.ts: settleInterruptedMapping runs in the attempt's durable
  order, so a stream cancel decides and evicts after any store write
  the request already has in flight, and keeps #1480's
  interrupted-turn marking.
- E2E.md: both sections kept.
commits.messageHeadline: Merge main into fix/async-durable-store-writes

commits.messageBody:
With asynchronous JSON writes, the beforeEach in
cache-keepalive-runner.test.ts read the store before its mapping was
written, so the runner found no mapping and returned "stop" instead of
"retry", and afterEach removed the directory under the still-running
write.
commits.messageHeadline: test: await the keepalive runner fixture's session mapping

commits.messageBody:
…live them

Each advisor test created a proxy and never closed it. With asynchronous
JSON writes, the opportunistic session GC a request starts can still be
running when bun moves on to the next file, and it then raced
bookkeeping-store-contract.test.ts over that file's session-gc.json lock,
failing its migration on a "live residue" lock candidate. Closing the
backend after each test joins the sweep.
